claude.sample_unit: emergency department patients with acute heart failure (EHR application); plus simulated cohorts

links.outcome: Proportion of patients with missing risk factors preventing AI risk calculation, and submodel coverage
links.effect: 1434 (36.1%) had at least one missing STRATIFY risk factor; submodels allowed 864 (60.3%) of these patients to have risk calculated at ED admission.
links.quote: There are 1434 (36.1%) patients having at least one missing STRATIFY risk factor.

links.outcome: Need for local recalibration of prediction model on local EHR data
links.effect: Both intercept and slope of original STRATIFY model were recalibrated on local EHR data because event rate was much higher than the 12% in the original cohort.
links.quote: Based on the validation using the training dataset, both intercept and slope from the original STRATIFY model were recalibrated.

unlisted_practices: Submodel approximation approach for handling missing risk factors in EHR-implemented prediction models

models_evaluated: imputation by fixed chained equations approach

links.outcome: Robustness to missing inputs and heterogeneity
links.effect: Across 1000 simulations per scenario, preconditioning and imputation were stable; OSS rMSPE increased under heterogeneous means.
links.quote: Under the heterogeneous mean scenarios ( Figure 3A ), rMSPEs from preconditioning-based submodels and the imputation approach are quite stable, whereas rMSPEs from OSS-based submodels increase with the heterogeneity in mean.

links.effect: Of 129 submodels, 80 met eligibility; C-index 0.60-0.63, NPV 0.82-0.92, Brier 0.19-0.19.
links.quote: Among 129 submodels, 80 are selected with eligible performance, where C-index ranges from 0.60 to 0.63, NPV ranges from 0.82 to 0.92 and Brier score ranges from 0.19 to 0.19.

links.effect: Local EHR adverse-event rate was 25.9% and much higher than original 12%; intercept and slope were recalibrated.
links.quote: This is expected because the event rate from the retrospectively collected EHR data is much higher than the 12% event rate from the original STRATIFY cohort which requires patients’ consent.

links.effect: 1434 (36.1%) patients had at least one missing STRATIFY risk factor.
links.quote: There are 1434 (36.1%) patients having at least one missing STRATIFY risk factor.

unlisted_practices: Use preconditioning-based submodels to calculate risk when EHR risk factors are missing

links.outcome: inability to calculate risk prediction due to missing risk factors
links.effect: more than 30% of acute heart failure patients had at least one missing risk factor, preventing risk calculation in its original form
links.quote: Preliminary EHR data extraction of STRATIFY risk factors revealed more than 30% of AHF patients had at least one missing STRATIFY risk factor at the time of disposition decision making, and thus cannot have STRATIFY risk calculated in its original form.
